name: Acquired Elastotic Haemangioma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Acquired Elastotic Haemangioma

criteria.description: Solitary, slow-growing, asymptomatic red to violaceous plaque or patch on sun-exposed skin, typically forearms
Proliferation of thin-walled, dilated capillaries in the superficial dermis with prominent solar elastosis
Positive staining for endothelial markers (CD31, CD34) confirming vascular nature
No cytologic atypia or features of malignancy on histology

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of typical clinical lesion on sun-exposed skin plus histopathological confirmation of vascular proliferation with solar elastosis and absence of malignancy
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on histopathological examination due to clinical similarity with other vascular lesions.

skin changes on arms or dorsal hands

common.symptomName: Presence of solar elastosis in adjacent dermis

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of malignant basal cells with peripheral palisading on histology
Multiple cherry angiomas typically on trunk
Smaller, bright red papules rather than plaques
